Both ligands are jnk3-inactive (derived jnk3 ~0.01), so crossover between them cannot create activity - it would only reshuffle two inactive scaffolds. Ligand 1 is the better host: QED 0.75, SA 2.17, MW 378, and it already carries the Ar-NH-C(=O) amide spine common to JNK3 series. Its N1-phenyl on the pyrazole (atoms 4-9, attached to pyrazole N at idx 3 by a non-ring biaryl bond) is a plain lipophilic cap contributing nothing but logP. I will swap it for a 2-aminopyrimidin-4-yl group, the canonical ATP-site hinge binder (donor/acceptor pair at the pyrimidine N1/2-NH2). MW stays ~395, and the extra ring N plus NH2 should pull logP down from 3.6 toward the QED sweet spot.

The pyrazole N at idx 3 is an aromatic ring nitrogen; cutting its biaryl bond leaves it as an NH, so re-attaching anything there exceeds nitrogen valence. Anchor on carbon instead. Better target anyway: the tetrahydroisoquinoline (atoms 17-27) is ~150 Da of purely lipophilic bulk hanging off the glycine CH2 at idx 16, and it is why LogP is 3.6. Cut the non-ring CH2-N bond 16-17 to drop it, and put the 2-aminopyrimidin-4-yl hinge binder on the CH2 instead. That leaves Ar-NH-C(=O)-CH2-(2-aminopyrimidinyl): MW falls to ~320, LogP toward 2, the amide spine is preserved, and the aminopyrimidine donor/acceptor pair is installed - so QED and SA should both improve while jnk3 gets a real chance.
